scope: All eight written-language samples; four specifically selected daily-life sources; shared identity and removal chronology for Choctaw, Chickasaw, Pawnee and Blackfoot; overview and ending continuity language for all cards; independent decoding of the three Oklahoma records and Haida Gwaii in world-1492.json. This is a bounded review, not certification of all 96 passages or all 70 sources.
result: No substantive historical correction in checked claims. Three minor editorial/locator findings were sent to the author, who confirms they are being corrected.

identitySourcesChecked.finding: Remaining Mississippi communities and the 1945 constitution support a distinct continuing Mississippi Band; broad prehistoric identity claims elsewhere on the page were not adopted.
Nineteenth-century removal, 1834 constitution and rebuilding substantiate the Oklahoma phase. Shared narrative does not collapse the Mississippi and Oklahoma governments.
1837 Doaksville arrangement and principal removal period 1837 to 1851 support explicit separation from Choctaw identity and rejection of 1492 Oklahoma dating.

identitySourcesChecked.access: Direct timeout; full primary indexed extraction read
identitySourcesChecked.finding: Four named bands, 1874 land move and continuing government corroborate the broader Pawnee identity across imported aliases.
Removal in 1874 to 1875 and allotment in 1893 directly supported.
Four named Blackfoot nations support a confederacy-level narrative that explicitly avoids a single centralized kingdom.
SGang Gwaay lies at 52 degrees 5 minutes 42 seconds north, south of the imported outline’s 53.2800-degree minimum. Public caveat is warranted.

geometryCheck.method: Read and independently delta-decoded TopoJSON arcs with transform.scale and transform.translate from data/hb/borders/world-1492.json; compared actual properties and all bounding boxes.
geometryCheck.finding: All match supplied geometry evidence. Public text appropriately warns that the Oklahoma chronology is wrong and the Haida outline incomplete. No geometry repair was performed or claimed. Mohawk remains separate from the broader Haudenosaunee card; Cree remains a regional grouping, not an empire.

limitations: No visual PDF inspection is claimed; writing was checked in extracted or indexed primary text. Parks Canada SGang Gwaay direct extraction did not expose the targeted shell-midden text, so that passage is outside this review’s certified subset. No full archaeological audit, independent survey of every border vertex, or live-site rendering was performed.

integrationReview.scope: Read final narratives and review findings. Independent checks have the limited scope recorded by each reviewer, not full historical certification. Metadata normalized; map coverage retained and no unverified successor links added.
